content: Hello! how can I help today?
I’m 73 and want to reduce my taxable income. Can I donate from my IRA instead of taking the full RMD?

Yes. You can use a **Qualified Charitable Distribution (QCD)** to donate up to **$100,000** per year directly from your IRA to a qualified charity. It counts toward your **RMD** and is **excluded from your taxable income** under IRC §408(d)(8).
How do I initiate the QCD properly?

You must request that your **IRA custodian** issue the check directly to the charity—**not to you**. Retain a copy of the check or letter showing the donation was made from the IRA to a qualified 501(c)(3).
Where do I report it on my return?

Report the **total IRA distribution** on Line 4a of **Form 1040**, and the **taxable amount (if any)** on Line 4b. Write ‘QCD’ next to line 4b to indicate the exclusion. Keep records in case of audit.
Is it better than just taking the RMD and donating cash?
Yes—donating through a QCD avoids raising your AGI, which can reduce **Medicare premiums, tax on Social Security, and itemized deduction phaseouts**. It’s the more strategic option if eligible.
